title: Intransitive Causatives: When the Causee Takes the Accusative (-t)

sections.title: Intransitive Base Verbs Become Transitive Causatives
sections.content: When the underlying verb is intransitive (having no direct object of its own, such as dolgozik 'works', gondolkodik 'thinks', várakozik 'waits', felel 'answers orally in class', vizsgázik 'takes an exam'), adding the causative suffix turns the verb into a direct transitive verb. Because the accusative slot (-t) is completely open, the person made to perform the action (the causee) takes the accusative suffix -t, NOT -val/-vel: A tanár megdolgoztatta a diákokat ('The teacher made the students work hard'); A kérdés elgondolkodtatta a kutatókat ('The question made the researchers think deeply').

sections.title: Comparing the Two Argument Patterns Side by Side
sections.content: The contrast between Lesson 2 and Lesson 3 is one of the hallmarks of B2 syntactic accuracy. Compare: A tanár feleltette a diákot ('The teacher quizzed the student / made the student recite' — intransitive base felel -> causee in -t) versus A tanár felmondatta a diákkal a leckét ('The teacher made the student recite the lesson' — transitive base felmondja a leckét -> theme in -t, causee in -val/-vel).

sections.title: Causee in -t (Intransitive Base) vs. Causee in -val/-vel (Transitive Base)
rows: Intransitive base (dolgozik): A mester alaposan megdolgoztatja a kutatókat.
The master makes the researchers work thoroughly.
Intransitive base (gondolkodik): Ez a paradoxon elgondolkodtatja az olvasót.
This paradox makes the reader pause and think.
Intransitive base (felel): A tanár ma három tanulót feleltetett.
The teacher quizzed three pupils orally today.
Transitive base (megír valamit): A tanár három tanulóval íratta meg a tesztet.
The teacher had three pupils write the test.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Ask yourself: Is there a separate direct object (-t) being acted upon? If NO (as with dolgoztat, elgondolkodtat, várat, feleltet), the person who is made to act takes -t!
